An indication as to whether edema is present.
An indication as to whether erythema is present.

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: Est Next Menstrual Period Start Date
EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Est Next Menstrual Period Start Date
Estimated Next Menstrual Period Start Date
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The approximate date of the first day of the next menstrual cycle.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Estimated Next Menstrual Period Start Date

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An approximate calculated date at which the conception event took place.
An approximate calculation of the delivery date.
An approximate calculation of the gestational age of the fetus.
A measurement of the distance between the pubic symphysis and the top of the palpable uterus.
An indication as to whether the subject is or has ever been pregnant.

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: Hosp Due to Pregnancy Complication Ind
EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Hosp Due to Pregnancy Complication Ind
Hospitalized Due to Pregnancy Complication Indicator
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An indication as to whether the individual was hospitalized due to a pregnancy complication.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Hospitalized Due to Pregnancy Complication Indicator

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An indication as to whether the female subject has ever had an induced abortion procedure.

An act or process of elucidation; explication, or explanation of the meaning of the event or thing via the assignment of objects from the domain to the constants of a formal language, truth-values to the proposition symbols, truth-functions to the connectives, other functions to the function symbols, and extensions to the predicates, if any. The assignments are result of human logic application and are not native to the symbols of the formal language.
The first day of the most recent menstrual cycle.
An indication as to whether the subject has ever delivered live-born offspring.
An indication as to whether a mass is present.
The age at which the first menstruation event occurred. (NCI)
The age at which permanent cessation of menses occurred. (NCI)
The status of a female with respect to menopause.
The length of time during which menses is expelled from the uterus.
A subjective description of the menstrual flow rate during a menstrual cycle.
The length of time of the menses cycle, measured from the beginning of one menstrual period to the beginning of the next.
A description of how an individual's menstrual cycle conforms to a consistent temporal pattern.
An indication as to whether any pregnancies resulted in miscarriages.
Description of the method by which a fetus is delivered.
An indication as to whether there are symptoms of motion tenderness.
A measurement of the total number of live birth events at which the gestational age of the neonate is 39 weeks and 0 days through 40 weeks and 6 days.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Number of Full Term Live Births

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A measurement of the total number of instances in which there has been a spontaneous termination of pregnancy (miscarriage) or elective termination of pregnancy.
A measurement of the total number of birth events experienced by a female.
A measurement of the total number of birth events at which the gestational age of the neonate is 37 weeks and 0 days through 38 weeks and 6 days.
A measurement of the total number of ectopic pregnancies experienced by a female subject.
A measurement of the total number of birth events (both live and dead) at which the gestational age of the neonate is 39 weeks and 0 days through 40 weeks and 6 days.
A measurement of the total number of induced abortions experienced by a female subject.
A measurement of the total number of fetal deaths (death of a fetus at 16 weeks, 0 days to 19 weeks, 6 days of gestation) experienced by a female subject.
A measurement of the total number of live-born offspring a female has delivered.
A measurement of the total number of pregnancy events experienced by a female.
A measurement of the total number of birth events (both live and dead) at which the gestational age of the neonate is less than 37 weeks and 0 days.
A measurement of the total number of live birth events at which the gestational age of the neonate is less than 37 weeks and 0 days.
A measurement of the total number of pregnancy events experienced by the female subject prior to the current pregnancy.
A measurement of the total number of spontaneous abortions (in which the fetus is less than 20 weeks gestational age) experienced by a female subject.

A measurement of the total number of birth events at which the fetus is of at least 20 weeks gestation, or of a birth weight of at least 350 grams if the gestational age is unknown, which is born without signs of life at the time of delivery, and with an Apgar score of zero at both one and five minutes.
The number of pregnancies reaching 20 weeks and 0 days of gestation or beyond, regardless of the number of fetuses or outcomes. (NICHD)
An indication as to whether there is the presence of peeling.
An indication as to whether the subject's pregnancy has been confirmed.
Findings observed at the end of a pregnancy.
An indicator as to whether a female is pregnant during the study period. (NCI)
An indication as to whether the subject or associated person is pregnant at the time the question is asked.
An indication as to whether the products of conception have been examined.
An indication as to whether a pustule is present.
An indication as to whether rash is present.
An indication as to whether the Skene's gland is abnormal.
An indication as to whether any pregnancies resulted in stillbirths.
An indication as to whether there are symptoms of tenderness.
A classification of the gestation duration of the pregnancy at the time of delivery.
The dimension between two surfaces of an object, usually the smallest dimension as opposed to the width or the length.
An indication as to whether an ulcer is present.
A description of the frequency at which vaginal bleeding and/or spotting has occurred.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Vaginal Bleeding and/or Spotting Frequency Description

CodeList.CDISCSynonym: Reproductive System Findings Test Name
CodeList.PreferredTerm: CDISC SDTM Reproductive System Findings Test Name Terminology

CodeList.Name: Respiratory Test Code

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist based on the test codes for physiological findings related to the respiratory system, including the organs that are involved in breathing such as the nose, throat, larynx, trachea, bronchi and lungs.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A measurement of the gas retention in a specified intrapulmonary space at the end of exhalation.
The quantity of gas that enters the alveoli during inspiration.
The total volume of gas in a specified airway or set of airways at a specified point in time in the respiratory cycle.
The total volume of gas in a specified airway or set of airways at a specified point in time in the respiratory cycle, expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The volume of the entirety of the airway tissue in a specified intrapulmonary region.
The volume of blood per unit time passing through a specified location, such as a point in a blood vessel or an entire organ.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Diffusion Capacity of Lung for CO
Transfer Factor of Lung for CO
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of the carbon monoxide that is transferred from inspired air into the pulmonary capillary blood.
The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide adjusted for hemoglobin concentration.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Hemoglobin Corrected Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value, adjusted for hemoglobin concentration.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Hemoglobin Corrected Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide expressed as a proportion of the alveolar volume, adjusted for hemoglobin concentration.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Hemoglobin Corrected Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide/Alveolar Volume Ratio

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The proportion of diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide to the alveolar volume expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value, adjusted for hemoglobin concentration.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Hemoglobin Corrected Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide/Alveolar Volume Ratio

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Mean Diffusion Capacity of Lung for CO
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The mean volume of the carbon monoxide that is transferred from inspired air into the pulmonary capillary blood.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Mean Carbon Monoxide Diffusing Capability Test

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide expressed as a proportion of the alveolar volume.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide/Alveolar Volume Ratio

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The proportion of the diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide to alveolar volume, expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide/Alveolar Volume Ratio

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An indication as to whether effusion is present.
The amount of three dimensional space occupied by the effusion fluid.
A measure of the resistance of a system to expand, i.e. the pressure change that is required to elicit a unit volume change in the lungs. Elastance is the reciprocal of compliance.
The maximum volume of air a subject can exhale from the lungs after a tidal exhalation.
The maximum volume of air a subject can exhale from the lungs after a tidal exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.05 Seconds over FVC
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The ratio of the volume of gas that is forcibly exhaled during the first 0.05 seconds following maximal inhalation to that of the forced vital capacity.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.05 Second to FVC Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.1 Seconds over FVC
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The ratio of the volume of gas that is forcibly exhaled during the first 0.1 seconds following maximal inhalation to that of the forced vital capacity.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.1 Second to FVC Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.2 Seconds over FVC
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The ratio of the volume of gas that is forcibly exhaled during the first 0.2 seconds following maximal inhalation to that of the forced vital capacity.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 0.2 Second to FVC Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The maximum volume of air an individual can exhale from the point of maximal inhalation.
The time required to exhale 63.2% of the total expiratory volume, as measured from the start of exhalation.
The mean forced expiratory flow rate at 25-75% of the forced vital capacity. (NCI)
The mean forced expiratory flow rate at 25-75% of the forced vital capacity as a proportion of the predicted normal value. (NCI)
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Flow at 25-75 Percent

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The mean forced expiratory flow rate at 50% of the forced vital capacity. (NCI)
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Flow at 50 Percent Forced Vital Capacity

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The forced expiratory flow rate during the first 0.05 second of a forced exhalation.
The forced expiratory flow rate during the first 0.1 second of a forced exhalation.
The forced expiratory flow rate during the first 0.2 second of a forced exhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first second following maximal inhalation.
A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the forced expiratory volume during the first second of exhalation to the largest observed expired volume during a forced vital capacity maneuver.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second to Forced Vital Capacity Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the forced expiratory volume during the first second of exhalation to the observed expired volume during the first six seconds of a forced vital capacity maneuver.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second to Forced Vital Capacity in 6 Seconds

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The proportion of total forced vital capacity that is expelled during the first second of a forced exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second Divided by Forced Vital Capacity

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Forced expiratory volume in one second as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The change in FEV1 following administration of a bronchodilator relative to the pre-treatment FEV1 value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second Reversibility

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the forced expiratory volume during the first second of exhalation to the largest observed expired volume during a slow vital capacity maneuver.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second to Slow Vital Capacity Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first three seconds following maximal inhalation.

A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the forced expiratory volume during the first three seconds of exhalation to the largest observed expired volume during a forced vital capacity maneuver.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume in 3 Seconds to Forced Vital Capacity Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Forced expiratory volume in three seconds as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 3 Seconds

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first six seconds following maximal inhalation.
Forced expiratory volume in six seconds as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 6 Seconds

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first 0.05 second following maximal inhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first 0.1 second following maximal inhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first 0.2 second following maximal inhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first half second following maximal inhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first 0.75 second following maximal inhalation.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Forced Expiratory Volume at Peak Expiratory Flow
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of gas that is forcibly exhaled at the peak of expiratory flow.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Forced Expiratory Volume at Peak Expiratory Flow

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The forced inspiratory flow rate at the point on the inspiratory flow-volume curve where 25 percent of the total volume of air has been inhaled.
The forced inspiratory flow rate at the point on the inspiratory flow-volume curve where 50 percent of the total volume of air has been inhaled.
The forced inspiratory flow rate at the point on the inspiratory flow-volume curve where 75 percent of the total volume of air has been inhaled.
The fastest rate of inspired air achieved during a forced inspiration maneuver.
The fastest rate of inspired air achieved during a forced inspiration maneuver expressed as a percentage of the expected result value for healthy individuals with similar characteristics.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Inspiratory Flow Maximum

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A measurement of the volumetric fraction of oxygen in the inhaled gas.
The volume of air that a subject can breathe in during the first second of inhalation after maximum exhalation.
The volume of air that a subject can breathe in during the first second of inhalation after maximum exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Percent Predicted Forced Inspiratory Volume in 1 Second

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The difference in lung volume between maximal expiration to residual volume followed immediately by full inspiration to total lung capacity during forceful inhalation.
The volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal exhalation. (NCI)
The functional residual capacity as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled following maximal inhalation.
The volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled during the first six seconds following maximal inhalation.
Forced vital capacity as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The instantaneous rate of air flow in the airway, expressed as the pressure difference between any given part of the airway and the alveoli; it is the reciprocal of airway resistance (Raw).
The maximum volume of air a subject can inhale into the lungs after a tidal exhalation (IRV plus TV).
The maximum volume of air a subject can inhale into the lungs after a tidal exhalation (IRV plus TV) as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The change in IC following administration of a bronchodilator relative to the pre-treatment IC value.
The measure of the force of the column of air in the conducting airways.
An indication as to whether infiltrates have occurred.

An act or process of elucidation; explication, or explanation of the meaning of the event or thing via the assignment of objects from the domain to the constants of a formal language, truth-values to the proposition symbols, truth-functions to the connectives, other functions to the function symbols, and extensions to the predicates, if any. The assignments are result of human logic application and are not native to the symbols of the formal language.
The maximum volume of air a subject can inhale into the lungs after a tidal inhalation.
The maximum volume of air a subject can inhale into the lungs after a tidal inhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The maximum volume of air an individual can inhale from the point of maximal exhalation.
The maximum volume of air an individual can inhale from the point of maximal exhalation as a percentage of the predicted normal value.

A representative measurement of the number of times the volume of air in the lung at the start of the washout (the Functional Residual Capacity) must be recycled to eliminate the tracer to the pre-defined endpoint.
The total volume of gas in a lobe of the lung at a specified point in time during the respiratory cycle.
The total volume of gas in a lobe of the lung at a specified point in time during the respiratory cycle, as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The basis for the determination that a malignancy is present.
An indication as to whether a malignancy is present.
The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated by exhaling against a mouthpiece, which is a measure of the strength of respiratory muscles. (NCI)

The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated by exhaling against a mouthpiece, which is a measure of the strength of respiratory muscles expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value. (NCI)
The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated during inhalation against a fully occluded airway, which is used to measure the strength of respiratory muscles. (NCI)

The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated during inhalation against a fully occluded airway, which is used to measure the strength of respiratory muscles expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value. (NCI)
The volume of oxygen per heartbeat consumed by the body while at rest.
The maximum rate of air flow expelled through the mouth, endotracheal, or tracheostomy tube during a cough. (NCI)
The maximum rate of exhalation.
The maximal flow achieved during the maximally forced expiration initiated at maximum inhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The change in PEF following administration of a bronchodilator relative to the pre-treatment PEF value.
The time from the start of the test until the subject reaches his maximum expiratory gas flow rate.
The maximum rate of inhalation.
A measurement of the ability of the lung to store energy, which is required for passive expiration.
An indication as to whether pneumonia has occurred.
The maximal flow achieved during the maximally forced inspiration through the nose initiated at maximum exhalation. (NCI)
A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the force per unit area (pressure) of oxygen dissolved in arterial blood to the percentage oxygen of an inhaled mixture of gasses.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Partial Pressure Arterial Oxygen to Fraction Inspired Oxygen Ratio Measurement

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The static elastic recoil pressure of the lungs at a given lung volume.
A measurement of respiratory tract resistance to airflow during inspiration and expiration.
A measurement of respiratory tract resistance to airflow during inspiration and expiration, as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
An assessment of the size difference in comparison to a baseline or previous value.
The ratio between the amount of carbon dioxide produced and oxygen consumed in one breath.
A calculated value based on all factors that influence the flow of gas from the airway opening to the alveoli, including airway resistance, and tissue resistance of the lung and chest wall. (NCI)
The volume of air remaining in the lungs after maximum exhalation.
The volume of air remaining in the lungs after maximum exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
A representation of the exponential function described by the Salazar-Knowles equation, and an estimation of a subject's inspiratory capacity.
The difference between the volume at total lung capacity and the hypothesized volume at a transpulmonary pressure of zero.
The reflection of the curvature of the upper portion of the deflationary limb of the pressure-volume curve.
A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the oxygen-hemoglobin saturation of a volume of blood to the volumetric fraction of oxygen in the inhaled gas.
A parameter used in functional respiratory imaging, derived by dividing the airway volume of a specified intrapulmonary region by the total volume of the same specified intrapulmonary region.

A parameter used in functional respiratory imaging, derived by dividing the airway volume of a specified intrapulmonary region by the total volume of the same specified intrapulmonary region, expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
A measurement of the airway conductance relative to lung volume. (NCI)
A measurement used to describe airway behavior irrespective of lung volume; it is calculated as airway resistance (Raw) multiplied by functional residual capacity (FRC).

A measurement used to describe airway behavior irrespective of lung volume; it is calculated as airway resistance (Raw) multiplied by functional residual capacity (FRC), as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after slow maximum inhalation.
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after slow maximum inhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The absolute volume of air contained in the thoracic cavity at any given point in time and at any level of alveolar pressure.
The total volume of air in the lungs after maximum inhalation.
The total volume of air in the lungs after maximum inhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
A measurement of the reflection of energy conservation within a given tissue.

The energy dissipated relative to the elastic energy stored in the tissue in a P-V cycle. (Fredberg JJ, Stamenovic D. On the imperfect elasticity of lung tissue. J Appl Physiol (1985). 1989 Dec;67(6):2408-19).
The volume of air moved into and out of the lungs during breathing at rest.
The volume of air moved into and out of the lungs during breathing at rest as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The rate at which oxygen is absorbed and utilized by any given tissue in the body.
The maximum rate of oxygen utilization at which oxygen uptake no longer increases and beyond which no level of effort can raise it.
The predicted maximum rate of oxygen uptake that is derived from physiological responses to submaximal exercise performance and is used as a measure of cardiorespiratory fitness.

An indication as to whether a malignancy is present.
The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated by exhaling against a mouthpiece, which is a measure of the strength of respiratory muscles. (NCI)
The greatest amount of pressure that can be generated during inhalation against a fully occluded airway, which is used to measure the strength of respiratory muscles. (NCI)
The maximum rate of oxygen utilization at which oxygen uptake no longer increases and beyond which no level of effort can raise it.

The fastest rate of inspired air achieved during a forced inspiration maneuver.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The mean volume of the carbon monoxide that is transferred from inspired air into the pulmonary capillary blood.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The rate at which oxygen is absorbed and utilized by any given tissue in the body.
The volume of oxygen per heartbeat consumed by the body while at rest.
A relative measurement (ratio or percentage) of the oxygen-hemoglobin saturation of a volume of blood to the volumetric fraction of oxygen in the inhaled gas.
The maximum rate of air flow expelled through the mouth, endotracheal, or tracheostomy tube during a cough. (NCI)
The maximum rate of exhalation.
The time from the start of the test until the subject reaches his maximum expiratory gas flow rate.
The maximum rate of inhalation.
The maximal flow achieved during the maximally forced inspiration through the nose initiated at maximum exhalation. (NCI)
The change in PEF following administration of a bronchodilator relative to the pre-treatment PEF value.
A measurement of respiratory tract resistance to airflow during inspiration and expiration, as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The total volume of gas in a specified airway or set of airways at a specified point in time in the respiratory cycle, expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide expressed as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The maximum volume of air a subject can exhale from the lungs after a tidal exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The volume of air that a subject can breathe in during the first second of inhalation after maximum exhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Forced vital capacity as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The functional residual capacity as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

The volume of air moved into and out of the lungs during breathing at rest as a proportion of the predicted normal value.
The total volume of air in the lungs after maximum inhalation as a proportion of the predicted normal value.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A measurement of the ability of the lung to store energy, which is required for passive expiration.
The static elastic recoil pressure of the lungs at a given lung volume.
An assessment of the size difference in comparison to a baseline or previous value.
The volume of air remaining in the lungs after maximum exhalation.
The ratio between the amount of carbon dioxide produced and oxygen consumed in one breath.
A representation of the exponential function described by the Salazar-Knowles equation, and an estimation of a subject's inspiratory capacity.
The difference between the volume at total lung capacity and the hypothesized volume at a transpulmonary pressure of zero.
The reflection of the curvature of the upper portion of the deflationary limb of the pressure-volume curve.
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after slow maximum inhalation.
A measurement of the airway conductance relative to lung volume. (NCI)
A measurement used to describe airway behavior irrespective of lung volume; it is calculated as airway resistance (Raw) multiplied by functional residual capacity (FRC).
A parameter used in functional respiratory imaging, derived by dividing the airway volume of a specified intrapulmonary region by the total volume of the same specified intrapulmonary region.
The absolute volume of air contained in the thoracic cavity at any given point in time and at any level of alveolar pressure.
The volume of air moved into and out of the lungs during breathing at rest.
A measurement of the reflection of energy conservation within a given tissue.

The energy dissipated relative to the elastic energy stored in the tissue in a P-V cycle. (Fredberg JJ, Stamenovic D. On the imperfect elasticity of lung tissue. J Appl Physiol (1985). 1989 Dec;67(6):2408-19).
The total volume of air in the lungs after maximum inhalation.
A calculated value based on all factors that influence the flow of gas from the airway opening to the alveoli, including airway resistance, and tissue resistance of the lung and chest wall. (NCI)

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The outward or visible aspect of an entity.

The volume consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per area per unit of time.
The quantity of a specified substance, which is based on catalytic activity, in a unit volume or weight of another substance.

The weight of a specified component divided by the number of entities.

The quantity, expressed as a weight, of a specified substance in a unit volume or weight of another substance.

The weight consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.
The quotient of the weight of one substance divided by the weight of another substance.
A statement about the form and/or structure of a target entity.
The individual test result relative to the median value of a reference set of test results.
An absolute count of the number of entities.
The number of specified entities per unit of area.
The number of specified entities in a unit volume or weight of a substance.
The number of component entities to the total number of entities.
The number of solute particles per liter of solution.
The pressure exerted by a single component of a mixture of gases.
The difference between two numbers divided by the average of the two numbers, multiplied by 100.
An indication of the presence of an entity which, if present, is identified.
An indication of the presence of an entity which, if present, is in an amount above a predetermined threshold.
The relationship in quantity, amount, or size between two entities or activities.
The quantity of a specified substance, which is based on catalytic activity, in a unit volume or weight of another substance, relative to a comparator.
The density of a specified substance, relative to a comparator.
The quantity, expressed as a weight, of a specified substance in a unit volume or weight of another substance, relative to a comparator.
The time of a specified activity, relative to a comparator.
A number or range of numeric values that assess and order a result or response for purposes of comparison.
The quantity, expressed in moles, of a specified substance in a unit volume or weight of another substance.
The molar amount of a component substance to the molar amount of the whole.
The molar amount of substance consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.
The quotient of the molar amount of one substance, divided by the molar amount of another substance.
The length of time during which something continues.
The quotient of one activity time interval divided by another activity time interval.
An identifiable class based on common distinguishable qualities.
The speed of an entity in a given direction.
The resistance of a liquid to sheer forces and flow. (NCI)
The amount of three dimensional space occupied by an object or the capacity of a space or container. (NCI)
The volume consumed, produced, excreted, or otherwise changed per unit of time.

CodeList.Name: SDTM Domain Abbreviation

Description.TranslatedText: A unique, 2-character domain code used in the regulatory submission process. The domain abbreviation is used consistently throughout the submission, i.e. in the dataset name, as the value of the domain variable within the dataset, and as a prefix for most variable names in the dataset. (CDISC Glossary)

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A two-letter prefix used to denote ADaM-compliant analysis datasets used for statistical analysis and reporting by the sponsor. These are submitted in addition to the data tabulation datasets.

An events domain that contains data describing untoward medical occurrences in a patient or subjects that are administered a pharmaceutical product and which may not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment.
An interventions domain that contains the agents administered to the subject as part of a procedure or assessment, as opposed to drugs, medications and therapies administered with therapeutic intent.
The adverse events domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The biospecimen domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The death details domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The demographics domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The exposure domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The laboratory test results domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Associated Persons Laboratory Test Results Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The medical history domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The questionnaires domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Relationship between Associated Persons and Subjects
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A dataset used to represent relationships between associated persons (individuals who are not study subjects, but about whom data is collected) and study subjects.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Relationship between Associated Persons and Subjects Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The reproductive system findings domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Associated Persons Reproductive System Findings Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The subject characteristics domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The subject status domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
The substance use domain for those persons associated with the study itself, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study.
A two-letter prefix used to denote an analysis dataset that is not compliant with a defined ADaM structure.
An events domain that documents biospecimen collection and storage information.
A findings domain that documents biospecimen handling information.
An events domain that contains clinical events of interest that would not be classified as adverse events.
An interventions domain that contains concomitant and prior medications used by the subject, such as those given on an as needed basis or condition-appropriate medications.
A special-purpose domain that contains comments that may be collected alongside other data.
A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the cardiovascular system, including the heart, blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.
A findings domain that contains the accountability of study drug, such as information on the receipt, dispensing, return, and packaging.
A findings domain that contains the diagnosis of the cause of death for a subject.
An events domain that contains data for device-related events.
A special-purpose domain containing information that identifies a specific device unit.

A special-purpose domain that includes a set of essential standard variables that describe each subject in a clinical study. It is the parent domain for all other observations for human clinical subjects.
A findings domain that contains the device characteristics that do not vary over the course of the study.
A special-purpose domain that contains the linkage of each subject to the device(s) to which they may have been exposed during the study.
An events domain that contains information encompassing and representing data related to subject disposition.
A events domain that contains the logistics and disposition information specific to a given device.

A findings domain that contains the measurements and settings that are intentionally set on a device when it is in use. These are characteristics that exist for the device, and have a specific setting for a use instance.
An events domain that contains protocol violations and deviations during the course of the study.
An interventions domain that contains a subject's exposure to a medical device under study.
An interventions domain that contains information about protocol-specified study treatment administrations, as collected.

A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the endocrine system, including the glands and cells that make hormones that are released directly into the blood and travel to tissues and organs all over the body.

A findings domain that contains ECG data, including position of the subject, method of evaluation, all cycle measurements and all findings from the ECG including an overall interpretation if collected or derived.

An interventions domain that contains the details of a subject's exposure to protocol-specified study treatment. Study treatment may be any intervention that is prospectively defined as a test material within a study, and is typically but not always supplied to the subject.
A findings domain that contains the findings about an event or intervention that cannot be represented within an events or interventions domain record or as a supplemental qualifier.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Findings About Events or Interventions Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A findings domain that contains data for named, stand-alone, task-based evaluations designed to provide an assessment of mobility, dexterity, or cognitive ability.

A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the gastrointestinal system, including the esophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, anus, liver, biliary tract and pancreas.
A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the hematopoietic system, including the bone marrow and lymph nodes involved in the production of blood.
A events domain that contains data for inpatient and outpatient healthcare events (e.g., hospitalization, nursing home stay, rehabilitation facility stay, ambulatory surgery).
A findings domain that contains those criteria that cause the subject to be in violation of the inclusion/exclusion criteria.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Inclusion Exclusion Criteria Not Met Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the integumentary system, including the epidermis, dermis, and all of their derivatives including hairs, nails, sudoriferous glands, and sebaceous glands.
A findings domain for assessments that determine whether a therapy induced an immune response.

A findings domain that contains laboratory test data such as hematology, clinical chemistry and urinalysis. This domain does not include microbiology or pharmacokinetic data, which are stored in separate domains.
A findings domain that represents non-host organisms identified including bacteria, viruses, parasites, protozoa and fungi.
An events domain that contains data that includes the subject's prior medical history at the start of the trial.
A findings domain that contains histopathology findings and microscopic evaluations.
A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the system of muscles, tendons, ligaments, bones, joints, and associated tissues.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Musculoskeletal Findings, Connective and Soft Tissue Findings Domain

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An interventions domain that contains information describing a subject's food product consumption.
A findings domain relevant to the science of the form and structure of an organism or of its parts.

A findings domain that represents drug susceptibility testing results only. This includes phenotypic testing (where drug is added directly to a culture of organisms) and genotypic tests that provide results in terms of susceptible or resistant. Drug susceptibility testing may occur on a wide variety of non-host organisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa and parasites.

A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the nervous system, including the brain, spinal cord, the cranial and spinal nerves, autonomic ganglia and plexuses.

A findings domain that contains tests that measure a person's ocular health and visual status, to detect abnormalities in the components of the visual system, and to determine how well the person can see.

A special-purpose domain containing information that identifies levels of taxonomic nomenclature of microbes or parasites that have been either experimentally determined in the course of a study or are previously known, as in the case of lab strains used as reference in the study.
A special-purpose domain that relates a set of genetic variations to an inference about the medical meaning of that set of genetic variations.
A findings domain that contains concentrations of drugs or metabolites in fluids or tissues as a function of time.
A findings domain that contains findings observed during a physical examination where the body is evaluated by inspection, palpation, percussion, and auscultation.
A findings domain for gene expression and genetic variation assessments.
A findings domain that contains supporting information for pharmacogenomics/genetics findings that applies to the entire test and not an individual findings result.
A dataset that identifies individual subjects included in a pool of subjects for which a single observation record (pool level) is captured.
A findings domain that contains pharmacokinetic parameters derived from pharmacokinetic concentration-time (PC) data.
An interventions domain that contains interventional activity intended to have diagnostic, preventive, therapeutic, or palliative effects.

A findings domain that contains data for named, stand-alone instruments designed to provide an assessment of a concept. Questionnaires have a defined standard structure, format, and content; consist of conceptually related items that are typically scored; and have documented methods for administration and analysis.

A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the respiratory system, including the organs that are involved in breathing such as the nose, throat, larynx, trachea, bronchi and lungs.
A dataset used to describe relationships between records for a subject within or across domains, and relationships of records across datasets.
A dataset used to represent relationships between study subjects.
A findings domain that contains physiological and morphological findings related to the male and female reproductive systems.
A findings domain for the assessment of disease response to therapy, or clinical classification based on published criteria.

An events domain that contains data describing untoward medical occurrences considered serious (SAE) in a patient or subjects that are administered a pharmaceutical product and which may not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment.

A special purpose domain that associates the subject with the medical conclusions contained in the pharmacogenomics biological state (PB) domain based on the observations reported in pharmacogenomics findings (PF) domain.
A findings domain that contains subject-related data not collected in other domains.
A special-purpose domain that contains the actual order of elements followed by the subject, together with the start date/time and end date/time for each element.
A special-purpose domain that is designed to record the timing, for each subject, of disease milestones that have been defined in the Trial Disease Milestones (TM) domain.
A findings about domain for submitting dermal responses to antigens.
A findings domain that contains general subject characteristics that are evaluated periodically to determine if they have changed.
An interventions domain that contains substance use information that may be used to assess the efficacy and/or safety of therapies that look to mitigate the effects of chronic substance use.

A type of adverse event that interrupts usual activities of daily living, or significantly affects clinical status, or may require intensive therapeutic intervention.

The mean diameter of the area of redness that forms around the site of an antigenic challenge to the skin.
The longest diameter of an area of hardness in the skin. (NCI)

The process of evaluating the wheal diameter in response to an allergen, based on a threshold size.
The longest diameter of the flat, circular, slightly raised area that forms around the site of an antigenic challenge to the skin.
The mean diameter of the flat, circular, slightly raised area that forms around the site of an antigenic challenge to the skin.

EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Current or Recent Employee or Volunteer in Homeless Shelter

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: CURRENT OR RECENT EMPLOYEE OR VOLUNTEER IN JAIL OR PRISON
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An individual who is presently or not long ago worked or offered to assist without pay at an institution where persons are confined for punishment and to protect the public.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Current or Recent Employee or Volunteer in Jail or Prison

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: CURRENT OR RECENT EMPLOYEE OR VOLUNTEER IN NURSING HOME
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An individual who is presently or not long ago worked or offered to assist without pay at a residential health care facility for persons with chronic illness or disability.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Current or Recent Employee or Volunteer in Nursing Home

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An individual without a stable or permanent residence within the last 365 days.

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: IMMIGRANT FROM HIGH TUBERCULOSIS PREVALENT AREA
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An individual that has migrated from a country with a high occurrence of tuberculosis.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Immigrant From High Tuberculosis Prevalent Area

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The state of being confined to jail or prison.
An individual that resided in a camp for those displaced from their homeland.

An individual that lives at a healthcare facility that provides rehabilitative, restorative, and/or ongoing skilled nursing care to patients or residents in need of assistance with activities of daily living.
An individual who moves from one location to another location within or outside of their homeland for work.

EnumeratedItem.CodedValue: REFUGEE FROM HIGH TUBERCULOSIS PREVALENT AREA
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: An individual that has fled a country for their own safety which has a high occurrence of tuberculosis.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Refugee From High Tuberculosis Prevalent Area

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Entry into one or more of the 22 countries that have a relatively high prevalence of tuberculosis cases.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Travel To High Burden Tuberculosis Country

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The state of not having a job.

CodeList.CDISCSynonym: Social Risk Factor
CodeList.PreferredTerm: CDISC SDTM Social Risk Factor Terminology

CodeList.Name: Specimen Collection Method

Description.TranslatedText: Terminology relevant to the method used in specimen collection.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A technique in which suction is used to remove bodily fluid or tissue.
The removal of tissue specimens or fluid from the living body for microscopic examination, performed to establish a diagnosis.
The removal of tissue with a curette (a spoon-shaped instrument with a sharp edge).
A technique in which material is cleared from the throat or lungs by coughing it up and spitting it out.
The removal of tissue specimens or fluid from the living body with a thin needle.
A technique in which the tip of a finger is pricked with a lancing device to obtain a small quantity of capillary blood.

A non-invasive specimen collection technique where cellulose acetate filter paper is applied to a body surface (e.g., ocular surface) to collect superficial epithelial cells, which can be air-dried or fixed and then stained for histological, immunohistological, or molecular analysis.
A technique in which hypotonic saline is inhaled, followed by expectoration.
A technique in which a fluid is introduced and collected from a body cavity or location.
A surgical procedure in which tissue is removed from the body.
A technique in which a tufted material on the end of a stick is rubbed against a surface.
A technique for specimen collection that utilizes an adhesive-based ribbon.

CodeList.CDISCSynonym: Specimen Collection Method
CodeList.PreferredTerm: CDISC SDTM Specimen Collection Method Terminology

CodeList.Name: Specimen Condition

Description.TranslatedText: The physical state or quality of a biological specimen.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: A specimen that has undergone agglutination, a process by which particles collect to form a cohesive mass or cluster.
A specimen that has undergone autolysis, or self-digestion by the specimen's own digestive enzymes. (NCI)
A specimen that has undergone calcification. (NCI)
A specimen that has become coagulated. (NCI)
A specimen that has undergone concentration to increase the content of a targeted entity.
The presence of any substance or organism that makes a preparation impure. (NCI)
A specimen that has become dessicated or dehydrated.
A specimen that is analyzed in the state that it was collected.
A specimen that has been subjected to and immobilized by severe cold. (NCI)
A specimen that has a gelatinous consistency. (NCI)
A specimen that has undergone the destruction of red blood cells followed by the release of the hemoglobin. (NCI)
A specimen that exhibits a yellowish pigmentation due to jaundice. (NCI)
A specimen that has become or appears milky.
A specimen that consists of or contains excessive amounts of fat and fatty substances. (NCI)
A specimen that has not undergone the destruction of red blood cells followed by the release of the hemoglobin.
A specimen that has been fixed and preserved in paraffin.
A specimen that has been kept or preserved at a low temperature in a refrigerator. (NCI)
A specimen that has been subjected to and adjusted to the average ambient temperature of a room, usually considered to be around 20 degrees C (68 degrees F). (NCI)
A specimen that has a regular, firm consistency and retains a definite size and shape.
A specimen that has changed from a frozen to a liquid or semi-liquid state.
A specimen that has an unanticipated odor.

CodeList.CDISCSynonym: Specimen Condition
CodeList.PreferredTerm: CDISC SDTM Specimen Condition Terminology

CodeList.Name: Specimen Type

Description.TranslatedText: The name and description of a biological specimen.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: The fluid that is abnormally collected in localized areas of damaged tissue within the body, usually composed of living and dead white blood cells, bacteria, and dead tissue.
Connective tissue consisting primarily of adipocytes (fat cells) and supporting structural matrix.
The gas from the alveoli of the lungs.
The fluid within the amniotic cavity which surrounds and protects the developing embryo. (NCI)
The watery fluid which is present in the anterior and posterior chambers of the eye. (NCI)

Oxygenated blood which is transported with nutrients to body tissues through the arterial system. The exception is blood within the pulmonary artery which carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. (NCI)
Blood present in the umbilical arteries at the time of delivery.
Capillary blood collected from a puncture site that has been warmed or treated with creams containing a hyperemic or vasodilatory agent to increase arterial blood flow.
Fatty tissue which is deposited in the inner lining of the arterial wall. (NCI)
A type of tear produced continually to keep the cornea moist; contains salts, water, and mucus.
Fluid composed of waste products, bile acids, salts, cholesterol, and electrolytes. It is produced by the liver and may be stored in the gallbladder (if present).

A liquid tissue with the primary function of transporting oxygen and carbon dioxide. It supplies the tissues with nutrients, removes waste products, and contains various components of the immune system defending the body against infection.
Calcified connective tissue that forms the skeletal components of the body. (NCI)
The tissue occupying the spaces of some bones. It consists of blood vessel sinuses and a network of hematopoietic cells.
Any cell with a single nucleus found in the bone marrow, for example lymphocytes, monocytes, mesenchymal stem cells and hematopoietic progenitor cells.
A liquid produced by the mammary gland.
The middle fraction of an anticoagulated blood specimen following separation by centrifugation. It contains most of the white blood cells and platelets.
A concretion of material in the body, usually composed of mineral salts. Representative examples include gallbladder stones, kidney stones, and salivary gland stones.
A mixture of arterial blood, venous blood and interstitial fluid, which is found in the capillaries.
A plasma sample that is prepared from capillary blood.
The striated muscle tissue of the heart enveloped by the epicardium and the endocardium. (NCI)
A cell sample that has been compacted by centrifugation.
The fluid that is contained within the brain ventricles, the subarachnoid space and the central canal of the spinal cord. (NCI)
A wax secreted by glands in the ear canal.
The watery fluid secreted from the glands and associated structures of the cervicovaginal region.
A metastatic cancer cell found in the peripheral blood. (NCI)
A thick, protein-rich substance secreted by the breasts during the second half of pregnancy and for a few days after birth before the breast milk comes in.
Blood present in the umbilical vessels at the time of delivery.
The clear portion of the blood that remains after the removal of the blood cells and the clotting proteins from the cord blood of a newborn baby.

The cells and connective tissue from the inner layer of the two main layers of the skin. The dermis has connective tissue, blood vessels, oil and sweat glands, nerves, hair follicles, and other structures. It is made up of a thin upper layer called the papillary dermis, and a thick lower layer called the reticular dermis.
The fluid which runs through a dialysis machine and captures, for discard or analysis, the excess water and waste from the blood stream through diffusion and ultrafiltration. (NCI)
The dialysis fluid which is collected from the peritoneal space and captures, for discard or analysis, the excess water and waste from the blood stream through diffusion and ultrafiltration. (NCI)
Normal or abnormal secretions expelled from a body location.
Partially digested gastric contents that are returned to the mouth or beyond via the vomit reflex present in some species.
A type of tear produced in response to negative or positive emotions; contains higher amounts of proteins and stress-related hormones in comparison to other tear types.
A specimen that consists of the cells and connective tissue of the endometrium.
The fluid collected from the lumen of the trachea.

The cells and connective tissue from the epithelial portion of the skin (cutis). It consists of the following layers: stratum corneum (horny layer), stratum granulosum (granular layer), stratum spinosum (prickle cell layer), and stratum basale (basal cell layer).
Any of the cells of the epithelium, which covers the body and lines its cavities and glands.
Cell specialized for oxygen transport, having a high concentration of hemoglobin in the cytoplasm and little else; biconcave, anucleate discs, 7nm diameter in mammals.
Expired air that has been condensed.
The air that moves out of the chest during expiration. It contains a higher percentage of carbon dioxide and a lower percentage of oxygen compared to the inhaled air. (NCI)
Accumulation of extravasated fluid containing inflammatory cells and fibrin. Necrotic debris and/or other cellular and extracellular components may also be present.
Liquid substances produced by the body.
The contents of the stomach that may include undigested food mixed with juices secreted by the gastric mucosal glands. (NCI)
The fluid produced by the stomach glands, composed of gastric acids and enzymes. (NCI)
The filamentous outgrowth of the epidermis. (NCI)

A tube-like invagination of the epidermis from which the hair shaft develops and into which the sebaceous glands open; the follicle is lined by a cellular inner and outer root sheath of epidermal origin and is invested with a fibrous sheath derived from the dermis. (NCI)
The liquid, solid or semi-solid lying below a liquid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a plasma sample. (NCI)
The liquid, solid or semi-solid lying below a liquid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a pleural fluid sample. (NCI)
The liquid, solid or semi-solid lying below a liquid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a serum sample. (NCI)
The extracellular fluid component found in the spaces between tissues. This excludes plasma and transcellular fluid.
A specific individual microbe and its genetically identical progeny separated on a single occasion from a sample taken from a host or culture system.
The keratin-producing cell of the epidermis that forms in the deep basal layer of the stratified epithelium.
Fluid introduced and collected from a body cavity or location by lavage or wash procedure.
Blood cells that are devoid of hemoglobin, capable of amoeboid motion and phagocytosis, and act as the principal components of the immune system.
Vaginal discharge occurring during the post-partum period. It consists of a mixture of blood, mucus, and placental remnants. (NCI)

Pulmonary surfactant lines the lung epithelium and lowers surface tension to prevent collapse at end-expiration. Deficiency of pulmonary surfactant results in respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants. Lung surfactant is synthesized in alveolar type II cells, stored in lamellar bodies and secreted via exocytosis. (NCI)

A clear, transparent, sometimes faintly yellow and slightly opalescent fluid that is collected from the tissues throughout the body, flows in the lymphatic vessels (through the lymph nodes), and is eventually added to the venous blood circulation. Lymph consists of a clear liquid portion, varying numbers of white blood cells (chiefly lymphocytes), and a few red blood cells. (NCI)
The cellular debris and fluid produced by lysis of cells.
The newborn's first intestinal discharge. It is a dark-green, thick substance composed of mucus, intestinal secretions, hair, and intestinal mucosa cells. (NCI)
The discharged blood from the uterus during the reproductive years. The discharge occurs approximately once a month. (NCI)
The de-oxygenated blood flowing into the right side of the heart, composed of a mixture of venous blood from the entirety of the systemic circulation.

A large, phagocytic mononuclear leukocyte produced in the vertebrate bone marrow and released into the blood; containing a large, oval or somewhat indented nucleus surrounded by voluminous cytoplasm and numerous organelles.
The thick fluid secreted by the mucus glands in the aerodigestive tract and the vagina. (NCI)
Tissue responsible for body and internal organ movement. Muscle tissue is composed of specialized contractile cells.
The cutaneous plate on the dorsal surface of the distal end of a finger or toe. (NCI)
A peripheral blood cell with a single nucleus, for example lymphocytes and monocytes.
The fluid within the peritoneal cavity.
The liquid secreted by the sweat glands. (NCI)
The fluid (acellular) portion of the circulating blood with retained clotting components.
The fluid that is produced from the movement of whole blood across a semipermeable membrane in response to a pressure gradient, removing blood cells and large proteins.
An irregular, disc-shaped structure in the blood that assists in blood clotting. Platelets are not blood cells, they are fragments of large bone marrow cells called megakaryocytes. (NCI)
A plasma sample that is prepared from whole blood, which has undergone a number of centrifugation steps to decrease the amount of platelets. (NCI)
A plasma sample that is prepared from whole blood, which has undergone a number of centrifugation steps to concentrate the amount of platelets. (NCI)
The fluid within the pleural cavity.
The serous membrane that lines the wall of the thoracic cavity and the surface of the lungs.
A slightly alkaline, white fluid secreted from the prostate and is a constituent of semen.
A yellowish substance produced during bacterial inflammation. It contains necrotic cells and cells fighting the infection. (NCI)
A type of tear produced in response to irritation from foreign particles, vapors, bright lights, or peppery substances; contains higher amounts of antibodies in comparison to other tear types.
Immature erythrocytes that have just undergone extrusion of their cell nucleus. They still contain some organelles that gradually decrease in number as the cells mature.
A clear liquid secreted by the salivary glands.
A thick, oily substance produced by the sebaceous glands located in the dermis. (NCI)
The fluid containing the spermatozoa, secreted by the testes and accessory reproductive glands of the male.
Part of the ejaculated fluid. It contains secretions from the seminal vesicles, Cowper gland, and prostate gland.
The clear portion of the blood that remains after the removal of the blood cells and the clotting proteins. (NCI)
The non-cellular portion of the circulating blood, with or without the clotting proteins present.
A specimen type consisting of serum or plasma or blood.
Voluntary, striated muscle tissue predominantly associated with the skeleton.
Tissue composed of three layers, epidermis, dermis and subcutis which protect underlying muscles and organs.
A white secretion of the sebaceous glands of the foreskin. (NCI)
Primarily involuntary, non-striated muscle tissue of the internal organs and blood vessels.
Refers to muscle, fat, fibrous tissue, blood vessels, organ parenchyma, or other supporting tissue of the body.
The male reproductive cell that is formed in the testicle. A sperm consists of a head, a body, and a tail that provides propulsion.
Material containing mucus, cellular debris, microorganisms and sometimes blood or pus. It is ejected through the mouth from the lungs, bronchi, and trachea. (NCI)
The material discharged from the bowel during defecation. It consists of undigested food, intestinal mucus, epithelial cells, and bacteria. (NCI)

Striated muscles are appendicular and axial muscles typically connected at either or both ends to the bony skeleton of the body. Striated muscle fibers contain a highly organized, contractile cytoskeletal apparatus with a striated microscopic appearance; muscle contraction is typically under voluntary control. (NCI)
The liquid lying above a liquid, solid or semi-solid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a cerebrospinal fluid sample. (NCI)
The liquid lying above a liquid, solid or semi-solid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a plasma sample. (NCI)
The liquid lying above a liquid, solid or semi-solid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a pleural fluid sample. (NCI)
The liquid lying above a liquid, solid or semi-solid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a serum sample. (NCI)
The liquid lying above a liquid, solid or semi-solid residue, which is separated by crystallization, precipitation or centrifugation of a serum or plasma sample. (NCI)
A heterogeneous and variable aggregate of body fluids, tissues, cells, microorganisms, and other materials that are collected from a swab biospecimen collection procedure.
The fluid within a joint capsule.
The fluid secreted by the lacrimal apparatus.
An anatomical structure consisting of similarly specialized cells and intercellular matrix, aggregated according to genetically determined spatial relationships, performing a specific function. (NCI)
The fluid that passes through the wall of the veins and capillaries to the surrounding tissues because of increased intravascular pressure. It has low protein content. (NCI)
A tumor sample, or entire tumor that is removed for examination.
The fluid produced by the kidneys.
Material separated from urine.

Deoxygenated blood containing urea and other waste products which is transported through the venous system to the heart and lungs. The exception is blood within the pulmonary vein which is oxygenated and travels from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. (NCI)
Blood present in the umbilical vein at the time of delivery.
A plasma sample that is prepared from venous blood.
The clear colorless transparent jelly that fills the posterior chamber of the eyeball. (NCI)

The nerve tissue forming the bulk of the deep parts of the brain and the superficial parts of the spinal cord. It is composed of nerve cell processes, i.e. extensions (axons), which connect various grey matter areas of the brain to each other and carry nerve impulses to and from the nerve cell bodies within the central nervous system (neurons). (NCI)

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire Past 3 Months Version - These are questions about other effects that your respiratory problems may have on you these days: Exercise is not safe for me.

EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: SGRQ Past 3 Months Version - Embarrassed Using Medication in Public

EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: SGRQ Past 3 Months Version - Treatment Interferes With My Life

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: SGRQ01-Take a Long Time to Get Washed
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire Past 3 Months Version - These are questions about how your activities might be affected by your respiratory problems: I take a long time to get washed or dressed.

CodeList.Name: Stent Thrombosis, Coronary ARC Grade Responses

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist relevant to the Academic Research Council grade for the probability that coronary artery stent thrombosis has occurred.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Includes acute ischemic symptoms at rest, acute post ischemic ECG, positive biomarkers and pathological evidence. Definite stent thrombosis is considered to have occurred when there is either angiographic or pathological confirmation. Angiographic confirmation is the presence of a thrombus at coronary angiography that originates in the stent or in the segment 5 mm proximal or distal to the stent, with the presence of at least 1 of 3 clinical criteria within a 48-hour time window: 1) acute onset of ischemic symptoms at rest; 2) new ischemic ECG changes that suggest acute ischemia; or 3) typical rise and fall in cardiac biomarkers. Pathological confirmation is evidence of recent thrombus within the stent determined at autopsy or via examination of tissue retrieved following thrombectomy. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical End Points in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

Possible stent thrombosis is considered to have occurred with any unexplained death more than 30 days after intracoronary stenting. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical End Points in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

Includes death within 30 days and myocardial infarction of stent territory. Probable stent thrombosis is considered to have occurred after intracoronary stenting in the following situations: 1) any unexplained death within the first 30 days; or 2) irrespective of the time after the index procedure, any MI that is related to documented acute ischemia in the territory of the implanted stent without angiographic confirmation of stent thrombosis and in the absence of any other obvious cause. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical End Points in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

CodeList.CDISCSynonym: Stent Thrombosis, Coronary ARC Grade Responses
CodeList.PreferredTerm: CDISC SDTM ARC Coronary Stent Thrombosis Grade Responses Terminology

CodeList.Name: Stent Thrombosis, Coronary, ARC Timing Responses

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist relevant to the Academic Research Council grade for the timing of the stent thrombosis after stent implantation.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: 0 to 24 hours after stent implantation. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical Endpoints in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

Greater than 30 days to 1 year after stent implantation. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical Endpoints in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

Greater than 24 hours to 30 days after stent implantation. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical Endpoints in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)

Greater than 1 year after stent implantation. (Cutlip DE, Windecker S, Mehran R, et al. Clinical Endpoints in Coronary Stent Trials : A Case for Standardized Definitions. Circulation. 2007;115:2344-2351)
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: ARC Stent Thrombosis Timing Very Late

CodeList.Name: Study Type Response

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist relevant to the role the study plays in determining the interventions a subject receives.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Studies that provide a means for obtaining an experimental drug or device for patients who are not adequately treated by existing therapy, who do not meet the eligibility criteria for enrollment, or who are otherwise unable to participate in another clinical study. Expanded Access studies include individual-patient IND, treatment IND, compassionate use, emergency use or continued access.

Studies in which individuals are assigned by an investigator based on a protocol to receive specific interventions. Subjects may receive diagnostic, therapeutic or other types of interventions. The assignment of the intervention may or may not be random. The individuals are then followed and biomedical and/or health outcomes are assessed.

Studies in which biomedical and/or health outcomes are assessed in pre-defined groups of individuals. Subjects in the study may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other interventions, but the investigator does not assign specific interventions to the subjects of the study.

Observational studies which include an organized system that uses observational methods to collect uniform data (clinical and other) prospectively for a population defined by a particular disorder/disease, condition (including susceptibility to a disorder), or exposure (including products, health care services, and/or procedures) and that serves a predetermined scientific, clinical, or policy purpose. Patient registries may be single purpose or on-going data collection programs that address one or more questions. (AHRQ)

CodeList.Name: Sudden Death Syndrome Type

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist that describes syndromes or conditions that put a subject at risk for sudden death.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Ventricular arrhythmia associated with Brugada syndrome
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in the absence of structural heart disease, associated with a baseline ECG pattern during sinus rhythm showing right bundle branch block with ST segment elevation in leads V1 through V3. It can also be characterized by documentation of ECG patterns associated with Brugada Syndrome, some of which may be unmasked when provoked with drugs. The most common genetic mutations identified for Brugada syndrome are in the sodium channel gene SCN5A.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Brugada Syndrome Ventricular Arrhythmia by ECG Finding

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Ventricular Tachycardia associated with syncope and/or cardiac arrest triggered by emotion or exercise in patients whose baseline ECG is normal.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia by ECG Finding

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation whose cause is unknown.
EnumeratedItem.PreferredTerm: Idiopathic Primary Ventricular Tachycardia/Ventricular Flutter by ECG Finding

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Ventricular arrhythmia associated with long QT syndrome
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Long QT Syndrome includes prolongation of the corrected QT interval beyond 440 ms for adult males, 460 ms for adult females and 50 ms in the presence of ventricular depolarization abnormalities (i.e., bundle branch blocks or IVCB more than 120 ms. A normal QT interval in a resting ECG with a failure to shorten with an increase in heart rate qualifies as Long QT Syndrome.
Different than the one(s) previously specified or mentioned. (NCI)

EnumeratedItem.CDISCSynonym: Ventricular arrhythmia associated with short QT syndrome
EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: Short QT Syndrome is characterized by a QT interval of less than or equal to 300 ms.

CodeList.Name: TIMI Flow Responses

Description.TranslatedText: A terminology codelist of acceptable values to describe TIMI Flow.

EnumeratedItem.CDISCDefinition: No perfusion. There is no antegrade flow beyond the point of occlusion. (Chesebro JH, Knatterud GL, Roberts R, et al, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) Trial, Phase I: a comparison between intravenous tissue plasminogen activator and intravenous streptokinase: Clinical findings through hospital discharge, Circulation 76, No. 1, 142-154, 1987)

Penetration without perfusion. Contrast material passes beyond the area of obstruction but "hangs up" and fails to opacify the entire coronary bed distal to the obstruction for the duration of the cineangiographic filming sequence. (Chesebro JH, Knatterud GL, Roberts R, et al, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) Trial, Phase I: a comparison between intravenous tissue plasminogen activator and intravenous streptokinase: Clinical findings through hospital discharge, Circulation 76, No. 1, 142-154, 1987)

Partial perfusion. The contrast material passes across the obstruction and opacifies the coronary bed distal to the obstruction. However, the rate of entry of contrast material into the vessel distal to the obstruction or its rate of clearance from the distal bed (or both) is perceptibly slower than its entry into or clearance from comparable areas not perfused by the previously occluded vessel (e.g., the opposite coronary artery or the coronary bed proximal to the obstruction). (Chesebro JH, Knatterud GL, Roberts R, et al, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) Trial, Phase I: a comparison between intravenous tissue plasminogen activator and intravenous streptokinase: Clinical findings through hospital discharge, Circulation 76, No. 1, 142-154, 1987)

Complete perfusion. Antegrade flow into the bed distal to the obstruction occurs as promptly as into the bed from the involved bed and is as rapid as clearance from an uninvolved bed in the same vessel or the opposite artery. (Chesebro JH, Knatterud GL, Roberts R, et al, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) Trial, Phase I: a comparison between intravenous tissue plasminogen activator and intravenous streptokinase: Clinical findings through hospital discharge, Circulation 76, No. 1, 142-154, 1987)
